text_elements.name: Text Placeholder 1
paragraphs: Bureau of Meteorology Australia - Deciles give an element a ranking, compared with the average for an area.
For example, choosing rainfall deciles will give a rainfall map showing whether rainfall is above average, average or below average for the time period and area chosen
To calculate deciles you first need to arrange your data, for example rainfall totals, in ascending order (from lowest to highest). i.e. to determine the median

Next, for deciles, divide the ranked data set into ten equal parts (i.e. ten blocks of 10%). The first group (the lowest 10% of rainfall totals on record) would be in decile range one (choose the top ranked of this range as ‘decile one’), the second group in decile range two, up to the highest 10% of rainfall totals being in decile range 10.

speaker_notes: Diagnosing problems in crops.

Lesions (LHS – possibly net blotch. Pyrenophora teres), Pustules (stem rust - eruption through epidermis Puccinia grammis - moist warm conditions / 30 C), powdery growth (Blumeria graminis f.Sp tritic – high humidity and temperatures (15-22C)

RHS - tip death many things can cause – cause by foliar nutrient (liquid N) – plants get over it (FlexiN high rate).
Colours - LHS - Pale colour on barley – symptomatic of lots of things – in this case N def. Old leaf -> N . Young leaf -> Sulphur.
Middle BYDV (barley yellow dawf virus) – transmitted by aphids (precipitation above 500m)

RHS - Interveinal chlorosis – Mn def in canola - also common in citrus Mn def. Similar to Magnesium deficiency. Location of Symptoms:Magnesium Deficiency: Symptoms appear on older, lower leaves first.
Manganese Deficiency: Symptoms appear on younger, upper leaves first.
Pattern of Chlorosis:Magnesium Deficiency: Interveinal chlorosis with green veins, often affecting the entire leaf blade in a more uniform manner.
Manganese Deficiency: Interveinal chlorosis with small, green specks or spots within the chlorotic areas, and often more pronounced in the upper leaves.
Group B herbicide Sulfonil urea (acts on growing point and nodes compress)
Compressed head caused by SU applied at different time – same herbicide different time. Residual effects.

During autumn, the cysts hatch following cold temperatures (below 15°C), stimulus from root exudates and moisture in the soil.
